skeleton:
Pan-Fried British Back Bacon

British · Easy · Serves 2 (6 rashers)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English's protein backbone: back bacon — the British cut, from the pork loin with a strip of belly attached, running meatier and leaner than American streaky — cooked slowly from a cold pan until the fat renders to crisp and the meat browns gently. This master writes the bacon component at its own scale, the full English's T−20 doctrine inherited, and the technique is the cold-pan start that renders before it seizes.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The bacon

  • the bacon
- The bacon from the refrigerator straight into the cold pan — no preheating, no added oil. The bacon's own fat is the cooking medium, and the cold start gives it time to render before the protein seizes.

Pan-Fried British Back Bacon

Prep: 2 minutes · Cook: 12 minutes · Total: 14 minutes · Serves 2 (6 rashers)

Ingredients

The bacon

  • 6 rashers back bacon (about 150 g total, each rasher
  • A nonstick or well-seasoned pan, ungreased — the bacon
  • 1 g fine sea salt (only if the bacon runs under-cured)
  • 5 g fresh parsley, chopped (optional garnish for the

Instructions

  1. The cold-pan start. The rashers laid in a single layer in a cold frying pan — the pan placed over medium-low heat and the bacon left undisturbed for the first 4 minutes. begun to turn translucent and the pan's floor carries a visible film of rendered fat — the rendering has begun, and the bacon's own medium is building. Checkpoint — the fat at the rashers' edges has
  2. The gentle turn and the finish. The rashers turned at the 4-minute mark; the heat maintained at medium-low; and the bacon cooked 6–8 minutes more, turned once more at the 8-minute mark, until the fat runs golden-crisp and the meat has browned evenly. golden (they snap at a bend), the meaty portions are browned and still yielding (not dried or curling), and the pan holds a pool of clear rendered fat — the bacon's full render, the technique's proof. Checkpoint — the fat strips are crisp and deep
  3. Drain briefly on kitchen paper and serve hot — on the full English, in a butty, or beside the scrambled eggs. crisp and the meat's yielding depth — the back bacon's two-texture identity, complete. Checkpoint — the first bite runs the fat's salted

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Cooked bacon holds 2 days refrigerated and re-crisps in a hot dry pan for 30 seconds a side. - The oven-baked master on this site runs the same bacon at 200 °C (390 °F) for 15–18 minutes — the batch-cook method for the full English's larger service.

methodSteps.chefsNote: the cold-pan doctrine is the British café's quiet inheritance from generations of bacon cooking: the cold start's low, slow approach renders the fat completely before the meat's proteins tighten, which produces the full English's ideal bacon — crisp-edged fat and yielding meat in the same rasher. The hot-pan method (the American instinct) sears the surface before the fat renders, producing rubbery fat and dry meat in the same rasher, and the difference is visible at the first bite.
